Ticket comment (patch set 2, bc354b6d32f): "the git grep in sunset_markers and the git show in engine_comparison decode with errors=replace"

Ticket Approach: "Add `encoding=\"utf-8\"` to each of the 85 calls, keeping any `errors=` the call already passes ... naming UTF-8 leaves POSIX behaviour byte-for-byte unchanged ... strict decoding (rather than `errors=\"replace\"`) keeps that equivalence and surfaces corrupt output instead of masking it."

dropped.finding: Patch set 2 added errors="replace" to two calls: the `git grep` in src/rebar/_commands/sunset_markers.py and the `git show HEAD:<path>` in src/rebar/llm/evals/engine_comparison.py. The ticket's Approach says to add only encoding="utf-8", keep only the errors= arguments a call already passes, and use strict decoding rather than errors="replace" so POSIX behaviour stays byte-for-byte the same. On Linux and macOS these two calls used to fail on invalid bytes and now silently replace them, so their behaviour changes beyond the ticket's encoding-only scope.
scenarios: A tracked file with non-UTF-8 bytes on a line that git grep matches: before this change the scan failed with UnicodeDecodeError on POSIX; now it returns text with replacement characters and the close guard goes ahead.

dropped.suggested_fix: Drop the added `errors="replace"` lines at src/rebar/_commands/sunset_markers.py:109 and src/rebar/llm/evals/engine_comparison.py:221 so both calls use strict UTF-8 as the ticket says. evidence: src/rebar/metrics/blame.py:42-49: `proc = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", repo_root, *args], capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", timeout=_GIT_TIMEOUT, check=False,)` (no errors=)
src/rebar/metrics/blame.py:50: `except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — best-effort: any git/OS error → no culprit` → `return None`
src/rebar/metrics/blame.py:160: `out = _git(repo_root, "blame", "-l", ref, "--", path)` — blame output includes each source line's content
src/rebar/metrics/blame.py:167: `tok = line.lstrip("^").split(" ", 1)[0]` — only the SHA token is used, so replacing undecodable bytes is lossless for the parse
Commit message: "The git grep in sunset_markers and the git show in engine_comparison carry arbitrary file content, so they decode with errors=\"replace\"" — blame was not given the same treatment
dropped.finding: metrics/blame.py `_git` runs `git blame -l ref -- path`, whose output contains raw file content. It now decodes with strict encoding="utf-8" and no errors="replace", so a source file with any non-UTF-8 byte raises UnicodeDecodeError. The broad except turns that into None, and culprit analysis silently returns no result for that file. On Windows this is new: cp1252 used to decode the output, and only the leading SHA token is parsed. It also breaks the commit's own rule that file-content calls use errors="replace".
scenarios: On Windows, a repo with a Latin-1 or binary-ish tracked source file: before, cp1252 decoded it and the SHAs were parsed; now _blame_file_commits returns None and no culprit is derived
On Linux, the same file already failed this way; errors="replace" would fix it on both platforms
dropped.suggested_fix: Add errors="replace" to the subprocess.run in blame._git. Alternatively, give _blame_file_commits its own call with errors="replace", as was done for sunset_markers and engine_comparison. Only the SHA prefix of each blame line is parsed.
